key_insight: Dopamine combines free-surface wave simulation, turbulence modelling and particle tracking in a Cartesian-grid framework for coastal flows.
engineering_relevance: The solver supports studies of wave interactions with seabeds and coastal obstacles, including small-scale turbulence and particle transport.
method: Staggered-grid LES with geometric volume-of-fluid free-surface tracking.
One-way-coupled Lagrangian tracking of heavy and buoyant particles.
Ghost-cell immersed boundaries with Vreman or AMD sub-grid-scale models.
evidence_signal: Analytical and benchmark comparisons assess wave dynamics and particle motion; reported two-fluid scaling efficiencies reach 77% strong and 73% weak at 512 CPU ranks relative to 64, with a single-GPGPU build verified against the CPU solver.
watch_item: One-way particle coupling neglects particle feedback on the flow, limiting applicability when particle loading significantly alters fluid dynamics.
paper_title: Dopamine: A Cartesian grid large-eddy-simulation framework for coastal ocean modelling of free-surface waves
